conviction_note: First standalone quarter after the ADI spin, with a new CEO and a new CFO and EPS/cash-flow guidance resuming on this call. The findings roughly cancel (+0.5 summed): Q3 HVAC-channel demand from Watsco and Carrier, a guide that assumes about 1% price, and low sentiment on one side; memory costs still rising into Q4 (TrendForce, and Alarm.com guiding Q4 hardware gross margin down 790bp) and the OEM security run-off on the other. The last two prints fell 18-20% on the guide line, so I set p_up 48 and abs_move 15 for a scaled -0.6. The small sign gap with impact_sum comes from first-guide reset risk under new management, which no single finding carries.
bar: Q3 2026 standalone revenue $705-730m and adjusted EBITDA $145-155m (company guide, Q2 release 2026-08-12, https://investor.resideo.com/news/news-details/2026/Resideo-Announces-Record-Second-Quarter-2026-Financial-Results-Initiates-Standalone-2026-Outlook/default.aspx). Revenue consensus is about $716.4m, near the guide midpoint, and non-GAAP EPS consensus is $0.45 against a $0.50 whisper (Earnings Whispers preview 2026-11-03, https://finviz.com/news/414516/resideos-first-standalone-quarter-tests-margins-as-input-costs-hit-hardest). The EPS bar has one source and the company gave no EPS guide, so the revenue/EBITDA guide is the usable bar. Standalone FY26 guide is $2.90-2.95bn revenue and $605-625m EBITDA. Against H1 standalone of $1,490m revenue ($752m+$738m) and $315m EBITDA ($158m+$157m), that implies Q4 revenue of about $680-755m and Q4 EBITDA of about $145-155m, flat to Q3 (same release, standalone bridge table).
positioning_check: Short interest 9.41M shares with 4.4 days to cover at the 2026-09-30 settlement (https://massive.com/quote/rezi). Benzinga puts it at about 10.1% of float and rising (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/REZI/sentiment). That is moderate, not a crowded short. Option put/call open-interest ratio is 0.12, call-heavy (baseline). The 25-delta skew is null in the baseline, so the option market makes no directional statement. ATM IV is 116.9% and the event-implied move 15.81%, with an ATM spread of 40% of mid, so the implied move is indicative only. Earnings Whispers says bearish sentiment rose from about 16% to 81% and the shares are down 13.5% since the last report (https://finviz.com/news/414516/resideos-first-standalone-quarter-tests-margins-as-input-costs-hit-hardest). Run-up is +16.1% over 20 days and +0.2% over 5 days; the stock is 33% below its 52-week high, though the spin distorts that.

findings.finding: Residential HVAC channel demand strengthened through Resideo's Q3. Watsco, the largest US HVAC distributor and a channel for Honeywell Home thermostats and controls, reported residential equipment +7% (units +5%, ASP +2%) and same-store sales +4% for the quarter ended 30 Sep, with momentum continuing into October. Carrier reported Americas residential up more than 30%. Resideo's own Q2 call said HVAC-distribution demand for premium thermostats was ahead of expectations, and the Q3 revenue bar ($716m consensus, at the guide midpoint) does not obviously include a channel upturn.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Pre-spin history only. Q4 2025 (2026-02-24) was a revenue beat with strong 2026 guidance and went +14.4%. Q2 2026 (2026-08-12) beat revenue and EPS but fell about 15-20% on the guide cut, so revenue beats have not saved the stock when the guide disappoints.
findings.why_not_priced: Watsco and Carrier reported after Resideo's last guide (2026-08-12). The only Resideo-specific consensus sits at the guide midpoint with no visible revision. If the market had priced a channel upturn, the revenue consensus would sit above the midpoint and the 20-day run-up would show a catalyst; neither is visible. The run-up is +16% but no news cause was found for it.
findings.independence: Carrier Q3: Americas residential more than 30%, no destocking (https://www.achrnews.com/articles/166938-carrier-residential-hvac-rebounds-but-price-hikes-loom). Carrier and Trane at the September Laguna conference said residential was far better than expected (https://www.achrnews.com/articles/166689-price-increases-remain-part-of-the-residential-hvac-outlook). Counterweight: Lennox Home Comfort organic revenue fell 1% in Q3 (https://www.panabee.com/news/lennox-earnings-q3-2026-report). Watsco's 'other HVAC products' line, closer to controls, grew only 2%. These are proxies; HVAC is one of several Resideo channels, alongside retail, electrical, security and OEM.

findings.finding: Memory-cost pressure is not peaking in the September quarter as Resideo told investors on 2026-08-12. TrendForce projects conventional DRAM contract prices up 10-15% QoQ in 4Q26, later revised to about 20%. Alarm.com, a direct residential connected-hardware peer, reported on 2026-11-05 and guided Q4 hardware gross margin to about 20.5% from 28.4% in Q3, citing memory costs rising ahead of planned price increases. Resideo's FY guide implies Q4 EBITDA of about $145-155m, flat to Q3, so a Q4/2027 margin outlook that has to absorb more cost inflation is at risk.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-08-12): input costs (memory, metals, PCBs) were part of the lowered outlook and the stock fell about 15% on the day, -20.4% in the baseline window (https://stockstory.org/us/stocks/nyse/rezi/news/earnings-call/rezi-q2-deep-dive-lower-guidance-and-segment-weakness-offset-solid-product-demand). Q3 2025 (2025-11-05) cut its outlook and went -23.75%.
findings.why_not_priced: Alarm.com's Q4 hardware-margin guide came five days before this print, and the TrendForce Q4 revision came on 2026-10-20, both after Resideo last spoke. If the market had priced a worse Q4 cost curve, the stock would have fallen into the print; instead it is +0.2% over 5 days. Partly priced: preview coverage already frames this as the input-cost quarter and sentiment is 81% bearish.
findings.independence: TrendForce, a different source: 4Q26 DRAM contract prices up about 20% QoQ (https://www.trendforce.com/news/2026-10-20/news-dram-prices-seen-rising-20-qoq-in-4q26-despite-slower-gains-ai-demand-tight-supply-support-outlook/). Lennox said Q3 tariff and inflationary costs were not fully offset by price (https://www.panabee.com/news/lennox-earnings-q3-2026-report). Counterweight: Resideo has known this since August and the Q4-implied guide is already flat, not up.

findings.finding: The non-core OEM security contract keeps running off. The H2 2026 headwind is $40-50m, and management said at Jefferies (2026-09-12) that this customer goes from $170-180m a year in early 2026 to $100-120m by mid-2027 and is largely wound down by 2028. Any 2027 framework given on this call starts with a revenue hole of roughly $60-70m (about 2% of revenue). Management says opex cuts offset most of the EBITDA effect (about $10m of gross margin).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The OEM loss was first disclosed with the Q2 guide cut (2026-08-12, -20.4% window). That move bundled it with input costs and the spin reset.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the H2 figure is in every preview. The 2027 step-down comes from one conference summary, so it is not in a filing or a press release. If it were fully priced, 2027 revenue estimates would show a visible OEM deduction; consensus 2027 figures found are stale pre-spin numbers ($7.98bn), so the post-spin 2027 bar is unclear.
findings.independence: Q2 deep dive, same company disclosure, so not independent (https://stockstory.org/us/stocks/nyse/rezi/news/earnings-call/rezi-q2-deep-dive-lower-guidance-and-segment-weakness-offset-solid-product-demand). Net of the rest: about 80% of revenue is repair/remodel and the branded channels grew in Q2.

findings.finding: The new CEO, Tom Surran, bought 15,000 shares in the open market at $20.46 on 2026-08-14 (about $307k), two days after the Q2 guide cut. The stock is now about 6% below his entry.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None measurable. Director Andrew Teich bought in 2025 at $30-34, ahead of later prints that went both ways.
findings.why_not_priced: Public for three months, so largely priced. It is filed as a small read on what the CEO who sets this first standalone guide thinks of the base. A kitchen-sink reset would be odd right after a personal purchase at $20.
findings.independence: The EDGAR filing index shows Form 4 filings on 2026-08-14/17/18 (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001740332&type=&dateb=&owner=include&count=40). Form 144 sale notices on 2026-09-02, 09-04, 10-02 and 10-20 point the other way; sellers not identified.

findings.finding: Low bar going in. Earnings Whispers bearish sentiment jumped from about 16% to 81%. Shares are down 13.5% since the last report and about $19 against analyst targets near $29-30. Short interest is 9.4M shares, 4.4 days to cover and rising. Options open interest is call-heavy (put/call 0.12). An in-line first standalone quarter could re-rate the stock off a depressed base.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 2025 (2026-02-24) went +14.4% after a run of negative sentiment. Washed-out names here have bounced on guides that were merely held.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the price, so this is about the asymmetry, not missed information. Short interest of about 6-10% of float is not crowded enough to be a squeeze mechanism by itself. Partly offset: the stock already rose 16% over 20 days without a found catalyst.
findings.independence: Short interest at the 2026-09-30 settlement (https://massive.com/quote/rezi). Analyst average target $29.83 as of Oct 30 (https://www.debelegger.nl/en/stock/REZI.US).

findings.finding: Management told the Jefferies conference (2026-09-12) that its forecasts assume only about 1% price, a conservative stance, while pricing actions announced in Q1/Q2 take time to show up. Peers are pushing large increases (Carrier 8% residential, Trane two rounds of up to 5%). The guided Q4 EBITDA of about $145-155m, flat to Q3 despite pricing catching up, leaves room for a held or firmed FY guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2026-02-24 print with a strong first 2026 outlook went +14.4%. The 2026-05-12 (-17.9%) and 2026-08-12 (-20.4%) prints reset guidance lower.
findings.why_not_priced: The 1% price assumption comes from a conference summary, not a release. If the market had priced pricing upside, the stock would not be trading at 81% bearish sentiment. Counterweight: it sits beside the memory finding, which argues that cost will absorb whatever price comes through.
findings.independence: Carrier 8% residential price increase (https://www.achrnews.com/articles/166938-carrier-residential-hvac-rebounds-but-price-hikes-loom). Trane two increases of up to 5% (https://www.achrnews.com/articles/166689-price-increases-remain-part-of-the-residential-hvac-outlook). This shares the Jefferies document with the OEM finding, but it is a different fact.

findings.finding: ADT, a large US residential security buyer of hardware and a plausible but unconfirmed identity for the OEM security customer moving in-house, agreed on about 2026-10-28 to be acquired by Thrive Holdings at $10 per share cash, a 46% premium. On 2026-11-03 it withdrew guidance and reported that more customers are buying hardware upfront.
findings.why_not_priced: Resideo has not named the customer, and ADT's results do not mention Resideo, so the link is unconfirmed. It is filed at zero so the panel can weigh it: a sector take-private at a premium is a valuation reference for residential security, and a change of control could change the in-house plan.

outside_window.finding: ADI Global Distribution, the spun-off business and a distributor of Resideo products, reports Q3 before the open on 2026-11-12. That is the day after this window closes, so its sell-through read on Resideo security and fire products comes too late for this trade.

The OEM security contract is largely wound down by 2028: revenue goes from $170-180m in early 2026 to $100-120m by mid-2027. The 2027-28 revenue effect lands beyond the window except through whatever 2027 framework this call gives (filed in findings at -0.5).

searched_and_found_nothing: 8-Ks since the Q2 print: none after 2026-08-12 in EDGAR (only Forms 3/4/144, 13G/A and S-3ASR/S-8 on 2026-08-07). No pre-announcement, no guidance update, no confirmed $200m debt repayment.
Analyst rating or target changes dated October-November 2026: none found. Latest dated actions are July 2026 (Morgan Stanley PT to $45, Zacks strong sell).
Cause of the +16% 20-day run-up: no company news found. The 2026-10-22 Apple Home thermostat software update is product PR.
Resideo 2026 distributor price-increase letter with an effective date: not found.
Q3 2025 standalone P&S comparables: the Q2 release gives standalone bridges for Q1 and Q2 2026 only.
Q2 2026 call transcript at stocktaper.com: HTTP 429 from that site (a site rate limit, not a tool budget refusal). Substituted with the MarketBeat, StockStory and Quartr summaries.
The Q2 2026 earnings presentation PDF could not be read as text.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with (null). The call-heavy open interest and the +16% 20-day run-up sit against 81% bearish sentiment. My findings offset and lean slightly to the guide-reset risk, so they neither confirm nor fight the run-up strongly. Pre-spin reaction history (median 15.3%) roughly matches the 15.8% implied move, and I kept abs_move at 15.
lessons_applied: Lesson 5 (proxies smaller): HVAC-channel finding trimmed from +0.8 to +0.6, since Watsco and Carrier are proxies and Lennox and Watsco's controls-adjacent line are weaker.

Lesson 3 (caveat reaches the number): memory finding trimmed from -1.5 to -1.2, because the flat Q4-implied EBITDA guide already embeds some cost and the risk is partly in previews. The pricing finding was trimmed from +0.7 to +0.6 for its counterweight against memory.
Lesson 7: short interest checked before the negatives (4.4 DTC, about 6-10% of float, not crowded), so the negatives were not shrunk further.
Lesson on untrustworthy history: reactions are pre-spin, but P&S drove the stock and the 15.8% implied move agrees, so abs_move stays at 15. Sum unchanged at +0.5; p_up and abs_move unchanged.
